finding: Autodesk's VIEWPORT-specific DXF table describes group 91 as a soft pointer reference to a viewport object. Autodesk's generic DXF group-code type table classifies 90-99 as 32-bit integers, and its Binary DXF documentation says binary values use the same group-code typing rules as ASCII DXF. The specific semantic role is documented, but the physical carrier/encoding conflicts with the generic type rule.

authoritative_references.title: VIEWPORT (DXF), AutoCAD 2021
authoritative_references.relevant_entry: Group 91: Soft pointer reference to viewport object (for layer VP property override); groups 335, 343 and 344 receive the same description.

authoritative_references.title: DXF Group Codes, ObjectARX 2027
authoritative_references.relevant_entry: 90-99 are 32-bit integer values; soft pointer IDs are in range 330-339.

authoritative_references.title: About Binary DXF Files, AutoCAD 2020
authoritative_references.relevant_entry: The type of binary data following a group code is determined by the same rules used to decode ASCII DXF.

current_implementation.classification: src/intern/dxfcode.h classifies 90-99 as I32 and gives group 91 no handle role; src/intern/dxfreader.cpp reads it as a 32-bit integer.
current_implementation.viewport_behavior: DRW_Viewport::parseCode rejects group 91; the typed layerOverrideReferences model and writer currently admit only 335, 343 and 344.
current_implementation.guard_reason: Changing the global classifier to a handle string would affect every group-91 use and contradict the generic integer rule; adding a viewport-only exception without producer evidence could make ASCII and Binary behavior inconsistent or encode a different physical value.

evidence_needed_to_implement: An authenticated native-producer ASCII and Binary DXF pair containing a VIEWPORT group-91 reference, with exact original file hashes and the referenced object handle identified independently.

A matching native read/save or independent parser observation that confirms whether group 91 is serialized as a decimal I32 or hexadecimal handle in each encoding and proves handle remapping/reference semantics.

Focused ASCII/Binary import, output, readback, wrong-target refusal, destination preservation and corrected retry controls; native paper-space layer-override behavior remains a separate qualification gate.
disposition: No parser, classifier, or writer change. Continue to reject group 91 rather than silently accepting an unverified representation. Do not promote VIEWPORT layer-override support claims.
limits: Documentation-only resolution of the semantic label is not physical wire proof, native activation evidence, or support qualification.
